title: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to the complete the following sentence:

His rather casual remarks on politics ___________ his lack of seriousness about the subject.
solution:
Answer: betrayed

"Betrayed" fits because it commonly means to reveal unintentionally or to disclose something that was previously hidden. In this sentence, the casual remarks made his lack of seriousness apparent.

  • Meaning of betrayed: revealed or exposed unintentionally.

  • Why it fits: The casual remarks "betrayed his lack of seriousness" — they revealed his attitude.

  • Why "masked" is wrong: "masked" means to hide or cover up, the opposite of reveal.

  • Why "belied" is wrong: "belied" means to give a false impression or to contradict; using it here would imply the remarks made him seem serious, which is not intended.

  • Why "suppressed" is wrong: "suppressed" means held back or restrained, which does not match the idea of making his lack of seriousness apparent.

title: Which of the following options is closest in meaning to
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Which of the following options is closest in meaning to the word Circuitous.
solution:
Answer: indirect

Definition: "Circuitous" means roundabout or not direct — taking a longer, winding route or using an indirect way of expressing something.

  • Why "indirect" is correct: Both words describe something that is not straight or direct. "Circuitous" emphasizes a winding or roundabout path, which matches "indirect."

  • Why "cyclic" is wrong: "Cyclic" means occurring in cycles or repeating; it does not convey being roundabout or indirect.

  • Why "confusing" is wrong: Something circuitous can be confusing, but "confusing" means unclear. It does not capture the specific idea of a long or winding route.

  • Why "crooked" is wrong: "Crooked" means bent, twisted, or dishonest; it does not mean roundabout or indirect.

Example: The driver's circuitous route took two hours instead of thirty minutes — it was indirect and roundabout.

Memory tip: Think of a circuit as a path that goes around — circuitous = taking a longer, winding path = indirect.

title: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence:

If we manage to ____________ our natural resources, we would leave a better planet for our children.
solution:
Answer: conserve — means to protect and use resources carefully.

  • conserve: To protect from loss or waste and to use sparingly; this verb commonly collocates with 'natural resources' and exactly expresses the idea of managing them wisely.

  • uphold: Means to maintain or support a principle or law; it does not convey the idea of protecting or saving resources.

  • restrain: Means to hold back or limit; we restrain consumption or behaviour, not the resources themselves, so it is not the right fit here.

  • cherish: Means to care for fondly or value emotionally; while positive, it is usually used for feelings or memories, not for the practical idea of managing natural resources.

Complete sentence: If we manage to conserve our natural resources, we would leave a better planet for our children.

title: The question below consists of pair of related words followed
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
The question below consists of a pair of related words followed by four pairs of words. Select the pair that best expresses the relation in the original pair.

Unemployed: Worker
solution:
Answer: fallow: land

Explanation: The original pair shows an adjective describing the condition or state of a noun. "Unemployed" is an adjective that describes a worker who does not have a job.

  • Match: "fallow" describes land that is left uncultivated (a specific condition of the land), which parallels how "unemployed" describes the condition of a worker. Both are adjective:noun pairs where the adjective denotes a particular state.

  • Why the others are incorrect:

  • "unaware: sleeper" is not a clear parallel because "sleeper" denotes someone who sleeps; the adjective "unaware" would pair more directly with a general noun like "person," and the semantic relation differs from the original.

  • "wit: jester" links a quality (wit) to a person who may possess it; this is a quality-to-person relation rather than an adjective describing the noun's current state.

  • "renovated: house" is adjective:noun, but it denotes an improved or altered condition rather than the kind of inactivity or lack-of-work condition shown by "unemployed: worker," so it is not as close a parallel.

title: Modern warfare has changed from large scale clashes of armies
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Modern warfare has changed from large scale clashes of armies to suppression of civilian populations. Chemical agents that do their work silently appear to be suited to such warfare; and regretfully, there exist people in military establishments who think that chemical agents are useful tools for their cause.

Which of the following statements best sums up the meaning of the above passage:

options.html: Modern warfare has resulted in civil strife.
Chemical agents are useful in modern warfare.
Use of chemical agents in warfare would be undesirable
People in military establishments like to use chemical agents in war.

solution:
Correct summary: People in military establishments like to use chemical agents in war.

Why this is best:

  • The passage says modern warfare has shifted toward suppression of civilian populations, setting the context for the rest of the statement.

  • It notes that chemical agents, which act silently, appear suited to that kind of warfare.

  • Crucially, the passage states that there exist people in military establishments who think chemical agents are useful tools for their cause; this is the main reported fact.

Why other choices are less suitable:

  • Saying chemical agents are useful states a fact; the passage only reports that some people believe they are useful, so that option is too strong.

  • Claiming modern warfare has resulted in civil strife is not supported directly by the passage; the passage emphasizes suppression of civilians, not the origin of civil strife.

  • Saying the use of chemical agents would be undesirable reflects the author's regret but is an evaluative statement; it is not as close to the passage's primary assertion that some military personnel favor chemical agents.

title: Which of the following options is the closest in the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which of the following options is the closest in the meaning to the word below:

Inexplicable
solution:
Answer: Incomprehensible. "Inexplicable" describes something that cannot be explained or is hard to understand; "incomprehensible" means not able to be understood, so it is the closest match.

Brief explanations of the choices:

  • Incomprehensible — means not able to be understood; this matches the sense of being unexplainable or difficult to grasp.

  • Indelible — means cannot be removed or forgotten (permanent); this is about durability, not explainability.

  • Inextricable — means impossible to separate or escape from; relates to entanglement or tight connection, not to being unexplainable.

  • Infallible — means incapable of making mistakes or being wrong; this concerns reliability, not lack of explanation.

Key tip: Focus on the core sense of the target word (unable to be explained or understood) and pick the option whose definition most directly matches that sense.

title: Choose the most appropriate word(s) from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Verb Tense or Verb Form Based on Clues
text:
Choose the most appropriate word(s) from the options given below to complete the following sentence.

I contemplated _________ Singapore for my vacation but decided against it.
solution:
Answer: "visiting" is correct.

Explanation: The verb "contemplate" is commonly followed by a gerund (verb+ing) when you mean considering doing something. Therefore "contemplated visiting Singapore for my vacation" correctly expresses that the speaker considered going there.

  • visiting — Correct because "contemplate" + gerund expresses considering an action (e.g., "I contemplated visiting Singapore").

  • to visit — Incorrect because "contemplate" is not followed by the infinitive in standard usage; use the gerund instead.

  • having to visit — Incorrect because it implies obligation or necessity (being required to visit), which is not the intended meaning of simply considering a vacation.

  • for a visit — Incorrect because this prepositional phrase cannot directly follow "contemplated"; you would need a verb phrase such as "contemplated going for a visit to Singapore."

Tip: Other verbs that typically take a gerund in this sense include consider, avoid, and postpone (e.g., "consider visiting").

title: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence.

If you are trying to make a strong impression on your audience, you cannot do so by being understated, tentative or ________.
solution:
Correct answer: restrained.

  • Why it fits: 'Restrained' means controlled, reserved, or subdued, which parallels 'understated' and 'tentative'. Together they describe qualities that prevent someone from making a strong impression.

  • Why the other choices are wrong: 'Hyperbolic' means exaggerated and would tend to create a strong impression, not prevent one.

  • 'Argumentative' means combative or prone to dispute; this does not convey being reserved or cautious.

  • 'Indifferent' means unconcerned or uninterested; while it might lessen impact, it does not match the specific sense of being modest or controlled implied by the sentence.

title: Choose the word from the options given below that is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word from the options given below that is most nearly opposite in the meaning to the given word

Amalgamate
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word with the meaning most nearly opposite to a given word. To find the best antonym, first fix the precise sense of the key word, then pick the option that reverses that exact action — not merely a word that is loosely “in the other direction.”

Application

“Amalgamate” means to combine or unite separate things into one whole (as when companies amalgamate, or metals are amalgamated). Its precise opposite is the action of taking one whole and breaking it apart into pieces.

Among the words offered, “split” names exactly that reversal — to divide a single unified thing into parts — so it is the most nearly opposite in meaning.

Why the others do not fit

  • “merge” — to blend things into one; this is a synonym of “amalgamate,” i.e. the same direction, not the opposite.

  • “collect” — to gather scattered items together; this again moves things toward union, not apart, so it is not an antonym.

  • “separate” — a near-antonym meaning to keep things apart, but it is a general word that need not start from a single combined whole; the exam keys the more precise reversal of “amalgamate.”

Cross-check

Replace the key word with the chosen option in a sentence: “The firms amalgamated” versus “The firms split” — the two sentences describe directly opposite events (one unit formed vs. one unit divided), confirming the choice.

title: Few school curricula include unit on how to deal with
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Few school curriculum include a unit on how to deal with bereavement and grief, and yet all students at some point in their lives suffer from losses through death and parting.

Based on the above passage which topic would not be included in a unit on bereavement?

options.html: how to write a letter of condolence
what emotional stages are passed through in the healing process
what the leading causes of death are
how to give support to a grieving friend

solution:
Correct answer: what the leading causes of death are. This topic concerns statistical information about mortality rather than how to cope with loss or support someone who is grieving.

Why the other topics would be included in a bereavement unit:

  • How to write a letter of condolence — teaches appropriate ways to express sympathy and provide comfort.

  • What emotional stages are passed through in the healing process — helps students recognise common reactions and understand that grief can be a normal, variable process.

  • How to give support to a grieving friend — offers practical skills for listening, being present, and helping someone through their grief.

In summary: a bereavement unit focuses on coping strategies, emotional understanding, and practical support. Information about leading causes of death is factual and epidemiological, so it does not fit the unit’s primary purpose.

title: Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below to complete the following sentence:

Despite several ––––––––– the mission succeeded in its attempt to resolve the conflict.
solution:
Answer: setbacks

Why this is correct:

  • The word "setbacks" means difficulties or obstacles that were encountered.

  • It collocates naturally with "despite": "Despite several setbacks, the mission succeeded..." expresses that success came in spite of problems.

Why the other choices are not suitable:

  • The word "attempts" causes awkward repetition with the later phrase "the mission succeeded in its attempt" and does not emphasize obstacles.

  • "Meetings" denotes gatherings rather than problems, so it does not create the intended contrast with success.

  • "Delegations" refers to groups of representatives and does not convey difficulties or hindrances, so it is not appropriate here.

title: Which one of the following options is the closest in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which one of the following options is the closest in meaning to the word given below?

Mitigate
solution:
Answer: Diminish

Meaning of "mitigate": to make something less severe, harmful, or intense.

  • Why "Diminish" fits: both words convey the idea of reducing or lessening the degree or severity of something.

  • Why the other choices do not fit: "Divulge" means to reveal or disclose; "Dedicate" means to devote; "Denote" means to indicate or signify. None of these relate to reducing severity.

Quick tip: When asked for a word closest in meaning, focus on the core action (here, reducing or lessening) and pick the option that matches that core.

title: Choose the grammatically INCORRECT sentence:
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the grammatically INCORRECT sentence:

options.html: They gave us the money back less the service charges of Three Hundred rupees.
This country’s expenditure is not less than that of Bangladesh.
The committee initially asked for a funding of Fifty Lakh rupees, but later settled for a lesser sum.
This country’s expenditure on educational reforms is very less.

solution:
Correct answer: The sentence "This country’s expenditure on educational reforms is very less." is grammatically incorrect.

Why it's incorrect:

  • "Very less" is not a standard or grammatical combination in English. The adverb "very" normally modifies adjectives (very low, very small) or adverbs, but it does not combine with comparative words like "less" in this way.

  • Use a correct alternative depending on meaning. For example: "This country's expenditure on educational reforms is very low." (if you mean the amount is small) or "This country's expenditure on educational reforms is much lower." (if you are comparing with another country).

Notes on the other sentences (brief corrections and confirmations):

  • They gave us the money back less the service charges of Three Hundred rupees.

    Suggestion: Use lowercase for numbers and add punctuation: "They gave us the money back, less the service charges of three hundred rupees." or "They returned the money to us, less a service charge of three hundred rupees."

  • This country’s expenditure is not less than that of Bangladesh.

    This is grammatically correct. A clearer alternative is: "This country's expenditure is at least as much as Bangladesh's."

  • The committee initially asked for a funding of Fifty Lakh rupees, but later settled for a lesser sum.

    Suggestion: Remove the article and lowercase the number: "The committee initially asked for funding of fifty lakh rupees, but later settled for a smaller sum."

title: Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below to complete the following sentence:

Suresh’s dog is the one ––––––––– was hurt in the stampede.
solution:
Answer: that

Explanation: The clause "was hurt in the stampede" is essential to identify which dog, so a restrictive relative pronoun is needed. "That" is the correct choice for animals/things in restrictive clauses without commas.

  • "that": correct — used for animals/things in a defining (restrictive) relative clause.

  • "which": generally introduces non-restrictive clauses and is usually set off by commas; not suitable here.

  • "who": used for people (subject); not the standard choice for an animal in this context.

  • "whom": object form for people; the clause needs a subject pronoun, so "whom" is incorrect.

Complete sentence: Suresh’s dog is the one that was hurt in the stampede.

title: Wanted Temporary, Part-time persons for the post of Field Interviewer
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Wanted Temporary, Part-time persons for the post of Field Interviewer to conduct personal interviews to collect and collate economic data. Requirements: High School-pass, must be available for Day, Evening and Saturday work. Transportation paid, expenses reimbursed.

Which one of the following is the best inference from the above advertisement?

options.html: Not designed to make the post attractive

solution:
Answer: Not gender-discriminatory

Explanation: The advertisement lists required qualification, availability for different shifts, and that transportation and expenses will be covered. It does not mention or imply any gender requirement or restriction, so the most supported inference is that the post is not gender-discriminatory.

  • Why the inference 'gender-discriminatory' is incorrect: There is no mention of gender or any exclusion based on gender in the ad.

  • Why the inference 'xenophobic' is incorrect: The ad contains no reference to nationality, origin, or any restriction against outsiders.

  • Why the inference 'not designed to make the post attractive' is incorrect: The ad offers incentives (transportation paid, expenses reimbursed) and clear scheduling details, which indicate attempts to make the position acceptable to applicants.

title: Which one of the following options is the closest in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which one of the following options is the closest in meaning to the word given below?

Nadir
solution:
Concept: A synonym question asks for the option whose meaning is closest to the given word. The method is to recall the precise sense of the headword, then match it against each option's meaning, remembering that an antonym (opposite-meaning word) is a common trap.

Applying it: 'Nadir' denotes the bottom-most or deepest point of something. It is used literally (the point on the sky directly beneath an observer, opposite the zenith) and figuratively (the worst or most depressed moment of a situation), as in "After the scandal, the team's morale reached its nadir." The option that captures this bottom-most sense is the right choice.

Contrasting the other choices:

  • 'Highest' is the direct opposite of 'nadir'; the term for the topmost point is 'zenith', so it is an antonym, not a synonym.

  • 'Medium' means a middle or average position, not an extreme, so it does not match the bottom-most sense of 'nadir'.

  • 'Integration' refers to combining parts (or a mathematical operation) and has no relation to the idea of a deepest or bottom point.

Result: The choice closest in meaning to 'nadir' is the one denoting the bottom-most point.

title: Complete the sentence: Universalism is to particularism as diffuseness is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Complete the sentence:

Universalism is to particularism as diffuseness is to _______________.
solution:
Concept: Verbal analogies of the form "A is to B as C is to D" hold when the relationship between A and B matches the relationship between C and D. Here that relationship is opposition: each term is paired with its conceptual opposite. The terms come from Trompenaars' framework of cultural dimensions, in which several traits are each set against a contrasting trait to form opposite pairs.

Applying it: Universalism (applying the same general rules to everyone) is opposed by particularism (varying the rules according to the specific relationship). The blank must therefore be the opposite of diffuseness. Diffuseness describes broad, overlapping relationships in which roles spill across many areas of life, so the answer is the term describing narrow, clearly bounded roles.

Comparing the choices:

  • specificity — narrow, well-defined roles where each interaction is kept separate; this is the exact opposite of diffuseness and completes the opposition pattern.

  • neutrality — belongs to a different Trompenaars pair (neutral vs affective), describing emotional restraint, not the breadth of a role.

  • generality — points toward broad rules, which sits on the universalism side rather than opposing diffuseness.

  • adaptation — means adjusting behaviour to circumstances and forms no opposite-pair with diffuseness.

Result: The term that completes the opposition with diffuseness is specificity.

title: Were you bird, you in the sky.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Modals of Future Intentions, Polite Requests and Hypotheticals
text: Were you a bird, you ___________________ in the sky.
solution:
Concept: A present unreal (second / hypothetical) conditional describes an imagined or contrary-to-fact situation in the present. Its structure is: if-clause in the past simple, and a result clause using "would" + base verb. The if-clause can be made more formal by inversion, dropping "if" and putting the verb first: "Were you ..." means exactly "If you were ...".

Application: Here the if-clause is the inverted "Were you a bird" (= "If you were a bird"), an imagined situation that is not real. The blank is the result clause, so it must take the form "would" + base verb:

  1. Identify the if-clause: "Were you a bird" is an inverted unreal condition in the present.

  2. Apply the rule: the result clause of a present unreal conditional uses "would" + base verb.

  3. Fill the result clause: "would fly" gives "Were you a bird, you would fly in the sky."

Contrast: the other choices carry the wrong modal meaning for an unreal present situation:

  • "shall fly" — "shall" marks a real simple future or formal intention, not an imagined / contrary-to-fact result.

  • "should fly" — "should" carries obligation, advice, or expectation, not the hypothetical result of an unreal condition.

  • "shall have flown" — a future-perfect form for an action completed in the future; it cannot pair with a present unreal condition.

title: Choose the grammatically INCORRECT sentence:
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the grammatically INCORRECT sentence:
solution:
The grammatically incorrect sentence is: “She is an European.”

Why?

The article “an” is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, not simply a vowel letter.

European begins with a consonant sound /y/ (“you-ro-pean”).

Therefore, the correct form is: “She is a European.”

All other options are grammatically correct.

title: After several defeats in wars, Robert Bruce went in exile
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
After several defeats in wars, Robert Bruce went in exile and wanted to commit suicide. Just before committing suicide, he came across a spider attempting tirelessly to have its net. Time and again, the spider failed but that did not deter it to refrain from making attempts. Such attempts by the spider made Bruce curious. Thus, Bruce started observing the near-impossible goal of the spider to have the net. Ultimately, the spider succeeded in having its net despite several failures. Such act of the spider encouraged Bruce not to commit suicide. And then, Bruce went back again and won many a battle, and the rest is history.

Which one of the following assertions is best supported by the above information?
solution:
Concept: In a “best supported / most valid inference” reading task, the correct choice is the one that the events stated in the passage directly entail — nothing more and nothing less. Reject a choice that is merely a familiar proverb loosely associated with the theme, and reject a choice that generalises beyond what the text actually claims.

Application: Trace what the passage actually states:

  • Bruce, after repeated defeats, is on the point of giving up (suicide).

  • He watches a spider fail again and again yet keep trying, and finally succeed.

  • This sight makes him abandon the idea of giving up and return to fight, eventually winning.

The single conclusion these events compel is that being in a desperate situation is not a sufficient reason to abandon hope — i.e. “No adversity justifies giving up hope.” The passage's whole point is the restoration of hope under hardship, so this is the inference it most directly supports.

Contrast with the other choices:

  • “Failure is the pillar of success” — a related-sounding maxim, but the passage frames failures as obstacles that were overcome by persistence and renewed hope, not as the foundation that builds success; it is an inference about cause that the text does not assert.

  • “Honesty is the best policy” — introduces a theme (truthfulness) that appears nowhere in the passage, so the text gives it no support at all.

  • “Life begins and ends with adventures” — a sweeping claim about the whole of life; the passage reports one turning-point episode and makes no such universal generalisation.

Cross-check: Re-read the final cause-effect chain — the spider's persistence directly leads Bruce to keep hoping and keep fighting. The choice that captures exactly that chain, without adding unstated claims, is “No adversity justifies giving up hope.”

title: Which of the following options is the closest in meaning
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the phrase underlined in the sentence below?

It is fascinating to see life forms cope with varied environmental conditions.
solution:
Answer: adapt to — meaning "adjust to" or "become suited to different conditions."

  • Why this matches the sentence: "cope with" means to manage or adjust to difficult or changing conditions, which is exactly what "adapt to" expresses.

  • Why the other choices are not suitable:

  • adopt to: "adopt" means to take up or start using something, not to adjust to conditions.

  • adept in: means skilled at something, which does not convey the idea of coping or adjusting.

  • accept with: is not idiomatic here and does not express adjusting to environmental conditions.

Example: Many species adapt to harsh climates by changing their behavior or physiology.

title: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence.

He could not understand the judges awarding her the first prize, because he thought that her performance was quite __________.
solution:
Answer: mediocre

Explanation: The sentence says he could not understand the judges awarding her the first prize, which shows he was surprised or disagreed with the decision. "Mediocre" means only average or of low quality, so it explains why he thought the award was undeserved.

Why the other words do not fit:

  • superb means excellent or outstanding, which would make the judges' decision understandable, not surprising.

  • medium means average, but it is less natural here than "mediocre," and the sentence implies a negative judgement stronger than just 'medium.'

  • exhilarating means exciting or thrilling, which would again make the award seem appropriate rather than surprising.

Tip: Look for the sentence tone—words that match the speaker's attitude (here, negative surprise) are the best choice.

title: In press meet on the recent scam, the minister said,
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Idioms, Phrases, Pharasal Verbs and Collocations
text: In a press meet on the recent scam, the minister said, "The buck stops here". What did the minister convey by the statement?
solution:
• The idiom “The buck stops here” means “I take full responsibility” or “The chain of blame or accountability ends with me.”

  • It was popularized by U.S. President Harry S. Truman, who kept this sign on his desk to show leadership and ownership of decisions.

  • Therefore, the correct inference is that the minister accepts responsibility for what has happened.

title: The Palghat Gap (or Palakkad Gap), region about km wide
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
The Palghat Gap (or Palakkad Gap), a region about 30 km wide in the southern part of the Western Ghats in India, is lower than the hilly terrain to its north and south. The exact reasons for the formation of this gap are not clear. It results in the neighbouring regions of Tamil Nadu getting more rainfall from the South West monsoon and the neighbouring regions of Kerala having higher summer temperatures.

What can be inferred from this passage?

options.html: The Palghat gap is caused by high rainfall and high temperatures in southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala
The regions in Tamil Nadu and Kerala that are near the Palghat Gap are low-lying
The low terrain of the Palghat Gap has a significant impact on weather patterns in neighbouring parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
Higher summer temperatures result in higher rainfall near the Palghat Gap area

solution:
Answer: The low terrain of the Palghat Gap has a significant impact on weather patterns in neighbouring parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

Reasoning:

  • The passage describes the Palghat Gap as lower than the surrounding hills and states this produces more rainfall in neighbouring Tamil Nadu from the southwest monsoon and higher summer temperatures in neighbouring Kerala.

  • From this information it is reasonable to infer that the gap’s lower terrain affects local wind and moisture flow, thereby influencing weather patterns in nearby regions.

Why the other interpretations are not supported:

  • The claim that the gap is caused by high rainfall and high temperatures is not supported; the passage says the gap leads to rainfall and temperature differences, not that climate created the gap.

  • The statement that neighbouring regions are low-lying cannot be inferred from the passage, which only describes the gap itself as lower than nearby hills.

  • The idea that higher summer temperatures cause higher rainfall near the gap is not supported; the passage links the gap’s terrain to both rainfall and temperature patterns but does not assert that temperature causes rainfall.

title: Geneticists say that they are very close to confirming the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Geneticists say that they are very close to confirming the genetic roots of psychiatric illnesses such as depression and schizophrenia, and consequently, that doctors will be able to eradicate these diseases through early identification and gene therapy.

On which of the following assumptions does the statement above rely?

options.html: Strategies are now available for eliminating psychiatric illnesses
Certain psychiatric illnesses have a genetic basis
All human diseases can be traced back to genes and how they are expressed
In the future, genetics will become the only relevant field for identifying psychiatric illnesses

solution:
Conclusion: Doctors will be able to eradicate certain psychiatric illnesses through early identification and gene therapy.

Premise: Geneticists say they are very close to confirming the genetic roots of psychiatric illnesses.

Key unstated assumption: Certain psychiatric illnesses have a genetic basis; if they do, then identifying genetic markers and applying gene therapy could plausibly allow eradication.

  • There is a genetic basis for certain psychiatric illnesses. This is the central assumption that connects confirming genetic roots to the possibility of eradication.

  • It is not assumed that effective gene-therapy treatments already exist; the argument speaks to a future possibility if genetic roots are confirmed.

  • It does not require that every human disease is genetic; the claim is limited to certain psychiatric illnesses.

  • It does not require that genetics will be the only relevant field in the future; other fields might still matter.

Why the selected assumption fits: If psychiatric illnesses have genetic roots, then confirming those roots enables the proposed chain: early identification of genetic markers followed by gene-based interventions. Without a genetic basis, the suggested eradication method (gene therapy) would not be applicable, so the argument necessarily assumes a genetic cause for certain psychiatric illnesses.

title: Choose the most appropriate phrase from the options given below
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the most appropriate phrase from the options given below to complete the following sentence.

India is a post-colonial country because

options.html: Indian Information Technology professionals have colonized the world
India does not follow any colonial practices
India has helped other countries gain freedom

solution:
A post-colonial country is one that was previously under colonial rule and later gained independence.
India fits this definition because it was a former British colony until 1947 and continues to deal with the political, social, and cultural effects of colonialism.

title: Who was coming to see us this evening?
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Verb Tense or Verb Form Based on Clues
text: Who ___________ was coming to see us this evening?
solution:
Correct sentence: Who did you say was coming to see us this evening?

Why this is correct:

  • The auxiliary 'did' is required to form a past simple direct question, so 'did you say' provides the correct question structure.

  • 'Who' is the subject of the subordinate clause 'was coming to see us this evening'. The sentence combines a main question clause ('did you say') with that subordinate clause.

  • Using 'you said' without 'did' does not invert the auxiliary and subject, so it does not form a proper direct question.

  • Adding 'that' (as in 'did you say that') is unnecessary here because the wh-word already introduces the subordinate clause; omitting 'that' is more natural.

  • Using 'had you said' (past perfect) changes the time reference and is not appropriate for this simple past question.

Conclusion: 'did you say' correctly forms the past simple question and fits the sentence structure, so it is the best choice.

title: Match the columns. Column eradicate distort saturate utilize Column misrepresent
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
solution:
Correct matching:

  • eradicate → destroy utterly

  • distort → misrepresent

  • saturate → soak completely

  • utilize → use

Explanation:

  • eradicate means to remove or destroy something completely, so it matches "destroy utterly".

  • distort means to change the true meaning or shape of something, so it matches "misrepresent".

  • saturate means to fill or soak completely, so it matches "soak completely".

  • utilize means to make use of something, so it matches "use".

title: The old city of Koenigsberg, which had German majority population
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text: The old city of Koenigsberg, which had a German majority population before World War 2, is now called Kaliningrad. After the events of the war, Kaliningrad is now a Russian territory and has a predominantly Russian population. It is bordered by the Baltic Sea on the north and the countries of Poland to the south and west and Lithuania to the east respectively. Which of the statements below can be inferred from this passage?

options.html: Kaliningrad was historically Russian in its ethnic make up
Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia
Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad, as that was its original Russian name
Poland and Lithuania are on the route from Kaliningrad to the rest of Russia

solution:
Answer: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia.

Why this follows from the passage:

  • The passage states the city is now Russian territory and has a predominantly Russian population.

  • It also lists Poland to the south and west and Lithuania to the east as bordering Kaliningrad, and the Baltic Sea to the north, which implies it is separated from mainland Russia (an exclave).

Why the other statements are not supported:

  • The claim that the city was historically Russian in ethnic make up is contradicted by the passage, which says it had a German majority before World War II.

  • The claim that Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad because that was its original Russian name is not supported; the passage only says it was renamed, without asserting any earlier Russian name.

  • The statement that Poland and Lithuania are on the route from Kaliningrad to the rest of Russia cannot be reliably inferred from the border information alone; the passage does not describe specific routes.

title: The number of people diagnosed with dengue fever (contracted from
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
The number of people diagnosed with dengue fever (contracted from the bite of a mosquito) in north India is twice the number diagnosed last year. Municipal authorities have concluded that measures to control the mosquito population have failed in this region.

Which one of the following statements, if true, does not contradict this conclusion?

options.html: A high proportion of the affected population has returned from neighbouring countries where dengue is prevalent
More cases of dengue are now reported because of an increase in the Municipal Office’s administrative efficiency
Many more cases of dengue are being diagnosed this year since the introduction of a new and effective diagnostic test
The number of people with malarial fever (also contracted from mosquito bites) has increased this year

solution:
Correct answer: The statement that the number of people with malarial fever has increased this year does not contradict the municipal conclusion.

Reasoning:

  • The municipal authorities infer that mosquito-control measures have failed because dengue cases doubled compared with last year.

  • To contradict that inference, a statement must provide an alternative explanation for the rise in dengue that does not involve an increase in the local mosquito population or transmission.

  • Imported cases or better detection/reporting offer such alternative explanations:

    • A high proportion of affected people returning from neighbouring countries could mean the increase is due to imported infections rather than failed local control.

    • More cases reported because of improved administrative efficiency could raise recorded numbers without an actual rise in infections.

    • Introduction of a new and more effective diagnostic test can increase detected cases by finding infections previously missed.

  • Why the increase in malarial fever does not contradict the municipal conclusion:

    Malaria is also transmitted by mosquito bites; a simultaneous rise in another mosquito-borne disease makes it more likely that mosquito abundance or biting rates have increased locally. That observation is consistent with the view that mosquito-control measures have failed.

    (Note: although different mosquito species transmit dengue and malaria, an increase in multiple mosquito-borne illnesses still supports a general failure of mosquito control unless additional information rules out species-specific factors.)

Conclusion: The rise in malarial cases supports the municipal conclusion about failed mosquito-control measures, while the other statements provide alternative explanations for the dengue increase and thus contradict that conclusion.

title: \(\underset{\text{I}}{\underline{\text{While trying to collect}}}\) an envelope \(\underset{\text{II}}{\underline{\text{from under the table,}}}\)
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
\(\underset{\text{I}}{\underline{\text{While trying to collect}}}\) an envelope \(\underset{\text{II}}{\underline{\text{from under the table,}}}\)\(\underset{\text{III}}{\underline{\text{Mr. X fell down}}}\)  and  \(\underset{\text{IV}}{\underline{\text{was losing consciousness.}}}\)

Which one of the above underlined parts of the sentence is NOT appropriate?
solution:
Answer: The phrase was losing consciousness is not appropriate.

Key reason: The past continuous "was losing consciousness" implies an ongoing, incomplete action. In this sentence the event is best presented as a completed action following the fall, so the simple past "lost consciousness" (or the phrase "became unconscious") is more appropriate.

  • Corrected sentence: While trying to collect an envelope from under the table, Mr. X fell down and lost consciousness.

  • Other parts are acceptable: the participle phrase "While trying to collect" correctly modifies Mr. X, the location phrase "from under the table" is grammatical (with "from beneath the table" as a stylistic alternative), and "Mr. X fell down" clearly describes the action.

title: If she how to calibrate the instrument, she done the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: If she _______________ how to calibrate the instrument, she _______________ done the experiment.
solution:
Correct answer: had known, could have

Why this is correct:

  • This is a third conditional (an unreal past). It describes a past situation that did not happen and its possible past consequence.

  • Form: If + past perfect (had + past participle), result = modal perfect (could/would/might + have + past participle).

  • Example: If she had known how to calibrate the instrument, she could have done the experiment.

Why the other choices are wrong:

  • knows, will have: Uses present and future-perfect forms, so it does not express a counterfactual past; it suggests a present/future situation instead.

  • knew, had: Uses simple past and past simple, which does not convey an unreal past hypothetical and results in a grammatically odd or incorrect meaning here.

  • should have known, would have: "Should have known" implies obligation, criticism, or regret rather than a neutral hypothetical condition. That changes the meaning from a simple counterfactual to blame or expectation.

Key tip: For unreal past conditions, use "had + past participle" in the if-clause and "could/would/might + have + past participle" in the result clause.

title: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the word “coherent”.
solution:
Answer: rambling

Key idea: "Coherent" means clear, logical, and well-organized. The opposite should describe something lacking clarity or logical order.

  • sticky — describes something adhesive or persistent; not about clarity or organization.

  • well-connected — aligns with the meaning of coherent (logical or connected), so it is not an opposite.

  • rambling — means disorganized or long-winded, lacking clear structure; this is the opposite of coherent.

  • friendly — refers to being kind or pleasant, which is unrelated to clarity or logical order.

Therefore, "rambling" is the best antonym because it denotes a lack of coherent structure and clarity.

title: Dance programme is scheduled for a.m. Some students are participating
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: A dance programme is scheduled for 10.00 a.m. Some students are participating in the programme and they need to come an hour earlier than the start of the event. These students should be accompanied by a parent. Other students and parents should come in time for the programme. The instruction you think that is appropriate for this is

options.html: Students should come at 9.00 a.m. and parents should come at 10.00 a.m
Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m. accompanied by a parent, and other parents and students should come by 10.00 a.m.
Students who are not participating should come by 10.00 a.m. and they should not bring their parents. Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m
Participating students should come before 9.00 a.m. Parents who accompany them should come at 9.00 a.m. All others should come at 10.00 a.m

solution:
Answer: Participating students should arrive at 9:00 a.m. (one hour before the programme) and must be accompanied by a parent. All other students and parents should arrive at 10:00 a.m., the start time of the programme.

  • Arrive early (9:00 a.m.): Participating students and their accompanying parent.

  • Arrive at start time (10:00 a.m.): All other students and parents.

Why: This makes sure participants are present and supervised for any preparation before the programme, while others arrive at the scheduled start time.

title: By the beginning of the th century, several hypotheses were
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
By the beginning of the 20th century, several hypotheses were being proposed, suggesting a paradigm shift in our understanding of the universe. However, the clinching evidence was provided by experimental measurements of the position of a star which was directly behind our sun.

Which of the following inference(s) may be drawn from the above passage?

(i) Our understanding of the universe changes based on the positions of stars

(ii) Paradigm shifts usually occur at the beginning of centuries

(iii)Stars are important objects in the universe

(iv) Experimental evidence was important in confirming this paradigm shift
solution:
Answer: (iv) only. Experimental evidence was important in confirming the paradigm shift.

Key evidence: The passage says that experimental measurements of the position of a star provided the clinching evidence for the paradigm shift.

  • Statement (i) — Our understanding of the universe changes based on the positions of stars: Not supported. The passage describes one measurement used as evidence, not a general rule that star positions change our understanding.

  • Statement (ii) — Paradigm shifts usually occur at the beginning of centuries: Not supported. The passage only notes the timing of this particular shift by the start of the 20th century; it does not assert a general pattern.

  • Statement (iii) — Stars are important objects in the universe: Not supported as a general inference. The passage mentions a specific star used as evidence but does not make a broad claim about the importance of stars.

  • Statement (iv) — Experimental evidence was important in confirming this paradigm shift: Supported. The passage explicitly credits experimental measurements as the clinching evidence.

Conclusion: Only statement (iv) is directly inferred from the passage.

title: Which of the following options is the closest in meaning
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the sentence below?

She enjoyed herself immensely at the party.

options.html: She had a terrible time at the party
She had a horrible time at the party
She had a terrific time at the party
She had a terrifying time at the party

solution:
Answer: She had a terrific time at the party.

Why: "Enjoyed herself" means she had a good time, and "immensely" means very much, so the sentence conveys a very positive, intense enjoyment.

  • The chosen paraphrase uses "terrific," which conveys a very positive and enthusiastic experience matching both the enjoyment and the intensity.

  • "She had a terrible time at the party" is the opposite in meaning; "terrible" describes a very unpleasant experience.

  • "She had a horrible time at the party" is also negative and does not match the original positive sentiment.

  • "She had a terrifying time at the party" implies fear or fright, not enjoyment, so it is not an appropriate paraphrase.

title: Which one of the following combinations is incorrect?
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Which one of the following combinations is incorrect?
solution:
Answer: Wheedle - Roundabout

Explanation:

  • Acquiescence - Submission: Both words refer to yielding or accepting quietly; they are synonyms.

  • Wheedle - Roundabout: "Wheedle" means to coax or persuade by flattery or cajoling. "Roundabout" means indirect. These meanings do not match, so this pairing is incorrect. A correct synonym for "wheedle" would be "coax" or "cajole."

  • Flippancy - Lightness: "Flippancy" denotes levity or a lack of seriousness, which aligns with the idea of "lightness" in tone. They are acceptable synonyms, though "flippancy" can have a more negative nuance.

  • Profligate - Extravagant: "Profligate" describes someone who is recklessly wasteful or excessively extravagant, so it matches "extravagant."

Conclusion: The incorrect combination is Wheedle - Roundabout because the meanings do not correspond.

title: Select the alternative meaning of the underlined part of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Idioms, Phrases, Pharasal Verbs and Collocations
text:
Select the alternative meaning of the underlined part of the sentence.

The chain snatchers took to their heels when the police party arrived.
solution:
Answer: "took to flight" is correct.

Meaning: The idiom "took to their heels" means to run away quickly or flee.

  • Why "took to flight" matches: Both phrases describe the act of fleeing quickly; "flight" here means escape.

  • Why "took shelter in a thick jungle" is incorrect: That option implies seeking cover in a specific place, not the immediate action of running away.

  • Why "open indiscriminate fire" is incorrect: This means to start shooting, which is unrelated to fleeing.

  • Why "unconditionally surrendered" is incorrect: Surrendering means giving up to authority, the opposite of running away.

Tip: Remember that "take to one's heels" is an idiom meaning to run away or flee at speed.

title: We our friend’s birthday and we how to make it
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: We __________ our friend’s birthday and we ________ how to make it up to him.
solution:
Correct sentence: We completely forgot our friend's birthday and we just don't know how to make it up to him.

  • Why “completely forgot” is preferred: placing the adverb before the verb (completely forgot) is the most natural and common word order in this context.

  • Why “just don't know” is correct: “just” here means “simply” or “only,” expressing that you simply do not know how to make it up.

  • Common error to avoid: “don't just know” changes the meaning to “do not only know,” which is not what you want in this sentence.

  • Stylistic tip: Use the full sentence with a possessive for clarity: “We completely forgot our friend's birthday and we just don't know how to make it up to him.”

title: Choose the statement where underlined word is used correctly.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the statement where underlined word is used correctly.

options.html: I write my experience in my personnel diary.
All personnel are being given the day off.

solution:
Answer: All personnel are being given the day off.

Explanation:

  • 'personnel' means staff or employees — it is used correctly in the sentence "All personnel are being given the day off."

  • Incorrect usage example: "The industrialist had a personnel jet."

    Correction: The industrialist had a personal jet.

  • Incorrect usage example: "I write my experience in my personnel diary."

    Correction: I write my experience in my personal diary.

  • Incorrect usage example: "Being religious is a personnel aspect."

    Correction: Being religious is a personal aspect.

Tip: 'personal' relates to a person or private matters; 'personnel' means staff or employees.

title: Generic term that includes various items of clothing such as
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: A generic term that includes various items of clothing such as a skirt, a pair of trousers and a shirt is
solution:
Answer: apparel — a general term for clothing items such as skirts, trousers, and shirts.

Why this is correct: 'Apparel' refers to garments or clothing as a category, so it correctly groups different items like a skirt, a pair of trousers, and a shirt.

Why the other choices are not correct:

  • Fabric: names the material or cloth used to make garments (for example cotton fabric), not the finished garments themselves.

  • Textile: refers to fibres, yarns, or the fabrics produced from them and the industry; it denotes material rather than finished clothing items.

  • Fibre: the raw material (such as cotton or wool) used to make yarns and fabrics, not a term for garments.

Quick tip: If you need a single word to refer to clothing items collectively, use 'apparel' or 'clothing'.

title: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:

options.html: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.
The report was useless to them because there were no needed information in it.
Since the report did not contain the needed information, it was not real useful to them.
Since the report lacked needed information, it would not had been useful to them.

solution:
The most suitable sentence is:

“Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.”

This sentence is grammatically correct and natural in usage.

  • “lacked needed information” is grammatically acceptable.

  • “was of no use” is a correct and idiomatic expression meaning “was useless.”

The other options contain grammatical or usage errors:

  • Option B: “information” is an uncountable noun, so “there were no needed information” is incorrect. It should be “there was no needed information” or, more naturally, “there was no necessary information.”

  • Option C: “real useful” is non-standard in formal English; “really useful” is required.

  • Option D: After would, the perfect construction must be would + have + past participle. Therefore, “would not had been” is incorrect; it should be “would not have been.”

Therefore, Option A is correct.

title: Extreme focus on syllabus and studying for tests has become
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Extreme focus on syllabus and studying for tests has become such a dominant concern of Indian students that they close their minds to anything ________ to the requirements of the exam.
solution:
Answer: extraneous — fits the sentence because it means 'irrelevant' or 'not essential'.

Explanation: 'Extraneous' commonly collocates with 'to' as in 'extraneous to the requirements', which precisely expresses that students ignore anything not relevant to the exam.

  • related: means connected or relevant. This is the opposite of the intended meaning.

  • outside: could work in different phrasing ('outside the requirements') but does not fit the exact collocation 'to the requirements' and is less idiomatic than 'extraneous'.

  • useful: means beneficial or helpful, which contradicts the context that students ignore things not required by the exam.

title: Select the pair that best expresses relationship similar to that
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to that expressed in the pair:

Children : Pediatrician
solution:
Key insight: the pair links a group of patients to the medical specialist who treats that group.

  • Identify the relationship: 'Children : Pediatrician' pairs a patient group (children) with the specialist dedicated to caring for that group.

  • Compare 'Females : Gynaecologist': This pairs a patient group (females) with the specialist who focuses on their reproductive health, so it mirrors the patient-group-to-specialist relationship.

  • Compare 'Kidney : Nephrologist': This links an organ (kidney) to the specialist who treats that organ, which is an organ-to-specialist relationship rather than a patient-group-to-specialist relationship.

  • Compare 'Skin : Dermatologist': This links a body part (skin) to its specialist, again an organ/body-part-to-specialist relationship, not the same as patient-group-to-specialist.

  • Compare 'Adult : Orthopaedist': Although 'adult' is a population, an orthopaedist treats musculoskeletal issues across ages and is not specifically the designated specialist for adults only, so this does not parallel the original relationship.

Conclusion: The best match is Females : Gynaecologist because it mirrors the patient-group-to-specialist relationship shown by Children : Pediatrician.

title: The Tamil version of John Abraham-starrer Madras Cafe cleared by
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The Tamil version of ________ John Abraham-starrer Madras Cafe _____ cleared by the Censor Board with no cuts last week, but the film’s distributors ______ no takers among the exhibitors for a release in Tamil Nadu _________ this Friday.
solution:
Answer: the, was, found, on

Explanation:

  • First blank — "the": The phrase names a specific film (Madras Cafe), so the definite article "the" is required rather than an indefinite article or a title.

  • Second blank — "was": The censorship action happened in the past and is described in the passive voice: the film "was cleared by the Censor Board."

  • Third blank — "found": The distributors experienced a past result: they "found no takers" among exhibitors. The past tense "found" fits the narrative.

  • Fourth blank — "on": Use "on" with days of the week or day references ("on this Friday"). "At this Friday" or other prepositions are not correct here.

Why the other word choices fail (brief):

  • "Mr." is a personal title and cannot serve as the determiner for a film name.

  • "a" makes the film sound indefinite, which is inappropriate when referencing a specific titled film.

  • "being" and the base form "find" are grammatically wrong here; the sentence needs past forms to describe completed actions.

  • The preposition "at" is not used with a day reference; use "on" instead.

title: Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order, he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite temperament. He was guilty of throwing away his wicket several times after working hard to lay a strong foundation. His critics pointed out that until he addressed this problem, success at the highest level will continue to elude him.

Which of the statements(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above passage?

(i) He was already a successful batsman at the highest level.
(ii) He has to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman.
(iii) He failed to make many of his good starts count.
(iv) Improving his technical skills will guarantee success.
solution:
Answer: The statements that can be inferred are that he needs to improve his temperament and that he failed to make many of his good starts count.

Reasoning:

  • The passage says that despite having the technical skills, he is unlikely to be a top batsman due to lack of requisite temperament, and critics say success at the highest level will continue to elude him until he addresses this.

  • Therefore it is valid to infer that he needs to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman.

  • The passage also states he was guilty of throwing away his wicket several times after working hard to lay a strong foundation. This supports the inference that he failed to convert many promising starts.

  • The claim that he was already a successful batsman at the highest level is not supported; the passage implies the opposite by saying he is unlikely to be so because of temperament.

  • The claim that improving technical skills will guarantee success is not supported either: the passage explicitly says he already has the technical skills, and identifies temperament (not technique) as the barrier, so a guarantee from technical improvement is not justified.

title: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage.

options.html: I will not leave the place until the minister does not meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister doesn’t meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.

solution:
Answer: I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.

Explanation: 'Until' introduces the time up to which an action continues. In this context the clause after 'until' should be affirmative and the verb must agree with the subject.

  • Why the correct sentence works: It uses 'until' to mark the time limit and uses the correct singular verb form 'meets' with the subject 'minister'.

  • Why the sentence using 'does not meet me' is wrong: Placing a negative ('does not') after 'until' creates an awkward or unintended meaning; the intended meaning is to wait until the meeting happens, so the affirmative 'meets' is needed.

  • Why the sentence using the contraction 'doesn't meet me' is wrong: The contraction still makes the clause negative, which is not appropriate with 'until' in this meaning; use the affirmative verb instead.

  • Why the sentence with 'minister meet me' is wrong: This is a subject–verb agreement error. 'Minister' is singular and requires 'meets'.

Corrected form: I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.

title: Rewording of something written or spoken is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: A rewording of something written or spoken is a ______________.
solution:
Answer: paraphrase — a rewording of something written or spoken.

Explanation: To paraphrase is to restate text or speech in your own words while preserving the original meaning.

  • paradox: a statement or situation that seems self-contradictory or counterintuitive; not a rewording.

  • paradigm: a model or example, not a restatement of words.

  • paraffin: a type of wax; unrelated to wording.

title: Archimedes said, “Give me lever long enough and fulcrum on
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Archimedes said, “Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I will move the world.”

The sentence above is an example of a ___________ statement.
solution:
Answer: figurative.

Explanation: The sentence is figurative because it uses exaggeration and imagery rather than stating a literal fact. Saying "I will move the world" emphasizes the power of a lever in a dramatic way; it is not a real claim that the speaker can physically move the planet.

Why the other choices are incorrect:

  • Collateral: means secondary or accompanying; it does not refer to a type of speech or figure of speech.

  • Literal: means exactly true or factual. This sentence is not meant to be taken literally, so 'literal' is incorrect.

  • Figurine: refers to a small statue or model and is unrelated to language or figures of speech.

title: The man who is now Municipal Commissioner worked as
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The man who is now Municipal Commissioner worked as ____________________.
solution:
Answer: a security guard at the university

  • Why this is correct: "a" introduces the job (a general role), and "the university" names the particular institution implied by the context. Together they form the natural phrase to describe a past occupation.

  • "The security guard at a university" is awkward because it pairs a definite article for the person with an indefinite reference to the institution, which changes the intended general meaning.

  • "A security guard at university" is not appropriate here because "at university" (without an article) typically means attending as a student, not working there.

  • "The security guard at the university" could be correct only if the man had previously been identified as that single, known guard. Without such prior identification, the indefinite "a security guard at the university" is the natural choice.

title: Nobody knows how the Indian cricket team is going to
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Idioms, Phrases, Pharasal Verbs and Collocations
text:
Nobody knows how the Indian cricket team is going to cope with the difficult and seamer-friendly wickets in Australia.

Choose the option which is closest in meaning to the underlined phrase in the above sentence.
solution:
Answer: put up with — This is the closest in meaning to "cope with."

  • Meaning of "cope with": manage or tolerate difficult situations.

  • "put up with" means to tolerate or endure, so it directly matches "cope with." Example: "They will have to put up with the seamer-friendly wickets."

  • Why the other choices are not correct:

  • "put in with": not an idiom meaning to cope or tolerate; does not fit the context.

  • "put down to": means to attribute something to a cause (e.g., "put down to bad luck"). It does not mean to manage or endure.

  • "put up against": is not the correct idiom for "cope with." While "be up against" can mean to face difficulties, the phrasing and meaning differ from "put up with."

title: Find the odd one in the following group of words.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Find the odd one in the following group of words.

mock, deride, praise, jeer
solution:
Answer: praise

Explanation:

  • mock, deride, and jeer all mean to ridicule, make fun of, or scorn someone.

  • praise means to express approval or admiration, which is opposite in meaning to the other three.

  • Therefore, praise is the odd one out because it has a positive meaning while the others are negative/derisive.

title: Computers were invented for performing only high-end useful computations. However,
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Computers were invented for performing only high-end useful computations. However, it is no understatement that they have taken over our world today. The internet, for example, is ubiquitous. Many believe that the internet itself is an unintended consequence of the original invention. With the advent of mobile computing on our phones, a whole new dimension is now enabled. One is left wondering if all these developments are good or, more importantly, required.

Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above paragraph?

(i) The author believes that computers are not good for us.

(ii) Mobile computers and the internet are both intended inventions
solution:
Answer: neither statement is logically valid.

Key points from the passage:

  • Computers were invented for high-end useful computations, but they have now "taken over our world."

  • The internet is described as ubiquitous, and the passage notes that many believe the internet was an unintended consequence of the original invention.

  • The author says readers are "left wondering" if these developments are good or required, which expresses uncertainty rather than an asserted belief.

Evaluate the first statement (The author believes that computers are not good for us):

This is not supported. The author questions whether developments are good or required but does not assert that computers are not good. Expressing doubt or posing a question is not the same as stating a belief that computers are harmful.

Evaluate the second statement (Mobile computers and the internet are both intended inventions):

This is not supported. The passage explicitly says many believe the internet was an unintended consequence, so describing the internet as an intended invention contradicts the passage. The passage does not state that mobile computing was an intended invention either.

Conclusion: neither statement can be logically inferred from the passage.

title: After Rajendra Chola returned from his voyage to Indonesia, he
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: After Rajendra Chola returned from his voyage to Indonesia, he ________ to visit the temple in Thanjavur.
solution:
Answer: wished (simple past)

Complete sentence: After Rajendra Chola returned from his voyage to Indonesia, he wished to visit the temple in Thanjavur.

  • Why simple past? The word "After" places both events in the past and shows sequence. Use simple past for a completed action that occurred after another past action.

  • Why not past perfect? "Had wished" would mean the wishing happened before another past event; here the wish happened after the return, so past perfect is unnecessary and incorrect.

  • Why not continuous tenses? "Was wishing" (past continuous) implies an ongoing action and sounds unnatural for a completed desire in this context. "Is wishing" (present continuous) does not match the past timeframe.

  • Tip: For two past events where one follows the other, use simple past for the later action unless you need to show an earlier past with past perfect.

title: Research in the workplace reveals that people work for many
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Research in the workplace reveals that people work for many reasons _______________ .
solution:
Correct answer: besides money

Explanation: Use "besides" to mean "in addition to." The complete sentence reads: "People work for many reasons besides money," which means they have motivations other than pay.

  • "money beside": wrong word order and misuse of "beside. It does not express "in addition to."

  • "beside money": "beside" usually means "next to" (physical position), not "in addition to."

  • "money besides": awkward and ungrammatical here. The correct phrasing is "besides money" or "for reasons other than money."

Grammar tip: "Besides" (with s) is used to mean "in addition to." It commonly appears before the noun phrase as in "besides money" or after the word it modifies as in "reasons besides money."

title: "The hold of the nationalist imagination on our colonial past
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Central Idea and Main Theme Identification
text:
"The hold of the nationalist imagination on our colonial past is such that anything inadequately or improperly nationalist is just not history."

Which of the following statements best reflects the author's opinion?

options.html: History is viewed through the filter of nationalism.
Nationalism has to be both adequately and properly imagined.

solution:
Correct answer: History is viewed through the filter of nationalism.

Explanation: The author says that the 'hold of the nationalist imagination on our colonial past' is so strong that anything that is not sufficiently nationalist is dismissed as not being history. This means the nationalist viewpoint determines what counts as historical account.

  • Why this matches: The phrase shows that nationalist interpretation acts as a filter or standard for historical legitimacy, so history is viewed through nationalism.

  • Why the other statements are wrong:

    • 'Nationalists are highly imaginative.' is a misreading: the passage refers to the influence of a nationalist perspective, not a claim about creativity.

    • 'Our colonial past never happened.' is incorrect: the author does not deny events occurred, only that nationalist standards exclude some accounts from being accepted as history.

    • 'Nationalism has to be both adequately and properly imagined.' is incorrect: the sentence criticizes the effect of a nationalist standard on historical acceptance, not giving guidance on how nationalism should be imagined.

title: Choose the option with words that are not synonyms.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the option with words that are not synonyms.
solution:
Key idea: identify which pair does not consist of synonyms.

  • aversion, dislike — These are synonyms: both mean a strong feeling of not liking something.

  • luminous, radiant — These are synonyms: both describe emitting or reflecting light; they convey brightness.

  • plunder, loot — These are synonyms: both mean to steal goods, often during war or disorder.

  • yielding, resistant — These are not synonyms: "yielding" means giving way, being flexible or compliant, while "resistant" means opposing or not giving in; they are essentially opposites.

Conclusion: The correct pair is yielding, resistant because they do not share the same meaning and are antonyms.

title: Saturn is to be seen on clear night with the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Saturn is ___________ to be seen on a clear night with the naked eye.
solution:
Correct answer: bright enough

Explanation: 'Enough' follows adjectives and adverbs when it means 'sufficiently'. In this sentence, place 'enough' after the adjective 'bright' and before the infinitive phrase 'to be seen'.

  • Rule: Put 'enough' after the adjective: adjective + enough

  • Correct sentence example: Saturn is bright enough to be seen on a clear night with the naked eye.

  • Why the other forms are wrong:

  • 'enough bright' — wrong word order; 'enough' must follow the adjective.

  • 'as enough bright' and 'bright as enough' — incorrect mixes of 'as...as' and 'enough'. Use 'as bright as' for comparisons or 'bright enough' to mean sufficient.

title: “We lived in culture that denied any merit to literary
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
“We lived in a culture that denied any merit to literary works, considering them important only when they were handmaidens to something seemingly more urgent – namely ideology. This was a country where all gestures, even the most private, were interpreted in political terms.”

The author’s belief that ideology is not as important as literature is revealed by the word:
solution:
Answer: 'seemingly'.

Explanation: The word 'seemingly' means 'appearing to be' and signals that the greater urgency of ideology is only apparent. The author uses this word to imply skepticism about ideology's claimed superiority over literature.

  • How this shows the author's view: 'seemingly' weakens the claim that ideology is genuinely more important; it marks that the priority is only on the surface.

  • Why the other words are incorrect:

  • The word 'culture' simply names the social setting and does not express the author's attitude about ideology versus literature.

  • The word 'urgent' describes how ideology was portrayed but does not itself indicate the author's skepticism about that portrayal.

  • The word 'political' refers to the interpretation of gestures, not to a comparison of importance between ideology and literature.

Takeaway: Look for words that express the author's stance (doubt, sarcasm, qualification). 'Seemingly' is a qualifier that signals the author's disbelief in the stated priority of ideology.

title: “From where are they bringing their books? bringing books from
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
“From where are they bringing their books? ________ bringing _______ books from _____.”

The words that best fill the blanks in the above sentence are
solution:
Correct answer: They’re, their, there

Filled sentence: They’re bringing their books from there.

  • First blank – They’re: contraction of "they are" (used before the verb "bringing").

  • Second blank – their: possessive adjective showing that the books belong to them.

  • Third blank – there: adverb of place indicating the location they are bringing the books from.

Common mistake:

  • "They’re" vs "Their" vs "There"

  • Tip: "They’re" = they are (use before verbs); "their" = possession (before nouns); "there" = place (adverb).

title: Investigation can sometimes yield new facts, but typically organized ones
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
“A _________ investigation can sometimes yield new facts, but typically organized ones are more successful.”

The word that best fills the blank in the above sentence is
solution:
Answer: meandering.

Explanation: The sentence contrasts a less organized investigation with organized ones. Therefore the blank should be filled by a word that means wandering or not methodical so the contrast is clear.

  • meandering — means wandering or not methodical; fits the intended contrast with organized investigations.
