  • timely — means occurring at a suitable time; does not contrast with organized, so it is not appropriate here.

  • consistent — means steady or regular; it does not convey a lack of organization and so does not fit the contrast.

  • systematic — means methodical or organized; inserting this would be redundant with "organized ones" and would remove the intended contrast.

Thus, "meandering" is the best choice because it creates the contrast with organized investigations that the sentence requires.

title: The expenditure on the project as follows: equipment Rs.20 lakhs,
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
subtopic: Verb Tense or Verb Form Based on Clues
text: The expenditure on the project _____ as follows: equipment Rs.20 lakhs, salaries Rs.12 lakhs, and contingency Rs.3 lakhs.
solution:
Answer: "breaks down"

Explanation: The subject "The expenditure" is singular, so the verb must be in the third-person singular present form. The phrasal verb "break down" means "be divided into parts," which fits the context of listing amounts.

  • Correct grammar: use third-person singular present: "expenditure breaks down".

  • Correct meaning: include the particle "down" so the verb means "is divided into parts," not simply "break."

  • Why other choices are wrong: the base form without an auxiliary is inappropriate here, and forms without "down" do not convey the intended division.

Complete sentence: The expenditure on the project breaks down as follows: equipment Rs.20 lakhs, salaries Rs.12 lakhs, and contingency Rs.3 lakhs.

title: The search engine’s business model around the fulcrum of trust.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The search engine’s business model ___________ around the fulcrum of trust.
solution:
Answer: "revolves" — correct.

Explanation: "revolves around" is a standard collocation meaning "is centered on" or "focuses on." It correctly conveys that the business model is built around the idea of trust.

  • Why "revolves" is correct: it naturally pairs with "around" to indicate centrality (e.g., "X revolves around Y" = X is centered on Y).

  • Why "plays" is incorrect: "plays" does not collocate with "around" to mean "is centered on." You could use "plays a role in" but that changes the structure and nuance.

  • Why "sinks" is incorrect: "sinks" implies falling or submerging and does not express being centered on something.

  • Why "bursts" is incorrect: "bursts" suggests exploding or breaking and is not used to mean "is centered on."

Alternative correct phrasings: "is centered on", "is built around", "focuses on".

title: Court is to judge as is to teacher.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: A court is to a judge as _____________ is to a teacher.
solution:
Answer: a school

Key idea: The analogy compares a workplace or location to the professional who works there.

  • Identify the relation: A court is the workplace/location associated with a judge.

  • Apply the same relation: The workplace/location associated with a teacher is a school.

  • Eliminate other choices: a student is a person taught by the teacher; a punishment is an action or consequence; a syllabus is a course outline — none of these are the location where a teacher works.

Therefore, "a school" best completes the analogy because it matches the same place-to-professional relationship.

title: Recent High Court judgement has sought to dispel the idea
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
“A recent High Court judgement has sought to dispel the idea of begging as a disease — which leads to its stigmatization and criminalization — and to regard it as a symptom. The underlying disease is the failure of the state to protect citizens who fall through the social security net.”

Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?

options.html: Beggars are lazy people who beg because they are unwilling to work
Beggars are created because of the lack of social welfare schemes
Begging is an offence that has to be dealt with firmly
Begging has to be banned because it adversely affects the welfare of the state

solution:
Key idea: The passage treats begging as a symptom of a larger problem: the state's failure to protect people who fall through the social security net.

  • The passage uses the words "symptom" and "underlying disease" to show that begging results from systemic failure rather than individual moral failure.

  • Therefore, the statement that beggars are created because of the lack of social welfare schemes is a valid inference: it restates the idea that gaps in social protection produce begging.

  • Claims that begging is due to laziness, that begging should be punished firmly, or that begging must be banned are not supported by the passage. In fact, the passage argues against stigmatization and criminalization.

Conclusion: The best inference is that lack of adequate social welfare or state protection contributes to the existence of beggars, so the statement asserting that beggars are created because of the lack of social welfare schemes is supported by the passage.

title: Raman is confident of speaking English six months as he
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Raman is confident of speaking English _______ six months as he has been practising regularly _______ the last three weeks.
solution:
Correct words: within, for

Explanation:

  • within — indicates a time limit or deadline (by or before a stated time). It fits here because it shows when he expects to be able to speak English (by six months).

  • for — indicates duration. 'For the last three weeks' correctly shows how long he has been practising up to now.

  • Why the other choices are not ideal:

    • 'during' is used for happening within a period but does not express achieving something by a deadline as clearly as 'within'.

    • 'since' requires a specific start point (for example, 'since March' or 'since last Monday'); 'since the last three weeks' is unidiomatic.

    • 'in the last three weeks' can sometimes describe activities that occurred at times inside that period, but 'for the last three weeks' better emphasises continuous practice.

Complete sentence: Raman is confident of speaking English within six months as he has been practising regularly for the last three weeks.

title: His knowledge of the subject was excellent but his classroom
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: His knowledge of the subject was excellent but his classroom performance was _______ .
solution:
Answer: extremely poor

Explanation: The conjunction 'but' introduces a contrast between the two parts of the sentence. The first part says his knowledge was excellent, so the second part must present an opposite idea about his classroom performance.

  • 'extremely poor' fits because it provides a strong negative contrast to 'excellent', matching the meaning signaled by 'but'.

  • 'good' is incorrect because it is positive and does not contrast with 'excellent'.

  • 'desirable' is incorrect because it means appropriate or wanted, not poor performance, and therefore does not create the required contrast.

  • 'praiseworthy' is incorrect because it is positive and means deserving praise, the opposite of a negative description.

Tip: Look for contrast words such as 'but', 'however', or 'yet' to determine whether you need an opposite or contrasting meaning in the blank.

title: Select the word that fits the analogy: Cook Cook Fly
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the word that fits the analogy:

Cook : Cook :: Fly : _______
solution:
Explanation: identify the relationship between the pair and apply it to the word "fly".

  • Determine the relationship: the first pair shows an action and the person who performs it (a cook is someone who cooks).

  • Apply the same relationship to the word "fly": we need the agent noun — the word for a person who flies.

  • Form the agent noun: the standard English form is "flyer". Other forms are incorrect because they denote the action ('flying'), the past tense ('flew'), or are nonstandard ('flighter').

Conclusion: the correct answer is flyer because it names the person who performs the action of flying.

title: The dawn of the 21st century witnessed the melting glaciers
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
The dawn of the 21st century witnessed the melting glaciers oscillating between giving too much and too little to billions of people who depend on them for fresh water. The UN climate report estimates that without deep cuts to man-made emissions, at least 30% of the northern hemisphere’s surface permafrost could melt by the end of the century. Given this situation of imminent global exodus of billions of people displaced by rising seas, nation-states need to rethink their carbon footprint for political concerns, if not for environmental ones. 

Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage ?

options.html: Nation-states are responsible for providing fresh water to billions of people.
Billions of people are responsible for man-made emissions.
Billions of people are affected by melting glaciers.

solution:
Correct inference: Billions of people are affected by melting glaciers. The passage explicitly says glaciers are "giving too much and too little to billions of people who depend on them for fresh water," which directly supports this conclusion.

  • Evidence from the passage: The phrase about glaciers affecting "billions of people who depend on them for fresh water" shows that a very large number of people are impacted by glacier changes.

  • Why the other statements are not supported:

  • The claim that nation-states do not have environmental concerns is not supported because the passage only says nation-states need to rethink their carbon footprint for political concerns, if not environmental ones; it does not assert absence of environmental concern.

  • The claim that nation-states are responsible for providing fresh water is not stated; dependence on glacier water is described, but responsibility for provision is not addressed.

  • The claim that billions of people are responsible for man-made emissions is not supported; the passage mentions man-made emissions as a cause of permafrost melt but does not attribute those emissions to billions of people.

title: Goods and Services Tax (GST) is an indirect tax introduced
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Goods and Services Tax (GST) is an indirect tax introduced in India in 2017 that is imposed on the supply of goods and services, and it subsumes all indirect taxes except few. It is a destination-based tax imposed on goods and services used, and it is not imposed at the point of origin from where goods come. GST also has a few components specific to state governments, central government and Union Territories (UTs).


Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage ?

options.html: GST is imposed on the production of goods and services.
GST does not have a component specific to UT.
GST is imposed at the point of usage of goods and services.

solution:
Answer: GST is imposed at the point of usage of goods and services.

Key reasoning:

  • The passage describes GST as a destination-based tax that is "imposed on goods and services used." This indicates the tax applies where goods or services are consumed (point of usage).

  • The passage also says it is "not imposed at the point of origin," which rules out statements that claim GST is levied at production or origin.

Why the other statements are incorrect:

  • "GST is imposed on the production of goods and services." This is incorrect because the passage emphasizes destination-based taxation at the point of use, not production.

  • "GST includes all indirect taxes." This is incorrect because the passage states GST subsumes all indirect taxes except a few, so it does not unconditionally include every indirect tax.

  • "GST does not have a component specific to UT." This contradicts the passage, which explicitly mentions components specific to Union Territories (UTs).

Conclusion: The statement that GST is imposed at the point of usage is supported directly by the passage's description of GST as destination-based and imposed on goods and services when used.

title: Consider the following sentences: Everybody in the class is prepared
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Consider the following sentences:

    (i) Everybody in the class is prepared for the exam.

    (ii) Babu invited Danish to his home because he enjoys playing chess.

Which of the following is the CORRECT observation about the above two sentences?

options.html: (i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is ambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is ambiguous

solution:
Answer: The correct observation is that the first sentence is grammatically correct and the second sentence is ambiguous.

  • Sentence (i): Everybody in the class is prepared for the exam. This is grammatically correct because 'everybody' is an indefinite pronoun treated as singular, so it correctly takes the singular verb 'is'.

  • Sentence (ii): Babu invited Danish to his home because he enjoys playing chess. This sentence is ambiguous because the pronouns 'his' and 'he' can refer to either Babu or Danish, so it is unclear whose home is meant and who enjoys playing chess.

    1. If the intended meaning is that Babu is the chess player and it is Babu's home: Babu invited Danish to Babu's home because Babu enjoys playing chess.

    2. If the intended meaning is that Danish is the chess player and it is Danish's home: Babu invited Danish to Danish's home because Danish enjoys playing chess.

title: Is to surgery as writer is to Which one of
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
_____ is to surgery as writer is to ________

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above sentence?
solution:
Key insight: determine the relation between the pair and apply it to the other pair.

  • Identify the relation for the first pair: a doctor is the person who performs surgery (agent performs an action).

  • Apply the same relation to the second pair: a writer is the person who produces a book (agent produces a product).

  • Therefore the matching pair is doctor (agent of surgery) and book (product of a writer).

Final answer: Doctor, book.

title: Some people suggest anti-obesity measures (AOM) such as displaying calorie
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Some people suggest anti-obesity measures (AOM) such as displaying calorie information in restaurant menus. Such measures sidestep addressing the core problems that cause obesity: poverty and income inequality.

Which one of the following statements summarizes the passage?

options.html: The proposed AOM addresses the core problems that cause obesity.
If obesity reduces, poverty will naturally reduce, since obesity causes poverty.
AOM are addressing the core problems and are likely to succeed.

solution:
Best summary: Anti-obesity measures such as displaying calorie information address the problem only superficially.

Key idea: The passage says these measures sidestep the core causes of obesity, which are poverty and income inequality.

  • The passage explicitly characterizes measures like displaying calorie information as sidestepping the core problems.

  • A correct summary should therefore say these measures are superficial rather than claiming they solve the root causes or will successfully reduce poverty.

  • Statements that claim the measures address core problems or that reducing obesity will reduce poverty misrepresent the passage.

Therefore, the statement that these anti-obesity measures are addressing the problem only superficially best summarizes the passage.

title: Gauri said that she can play the keyboard her sister.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Gauri said that she can play the keyboard __________ her sister.
solution:
Answer: as well as — this phrase means 'in addition to' or 'also', so the sentence states that Gauri can play the keyboard too, like her sister.

  • Key rule: Use 'as well as' to add someone or something (means 'also' or 'in addition to').

  • Comparatives: Do not use 'as better as' or 'as worse as'. For superiority or inferiority use 'better than' or 'worse than' (example: 'Gauri can play the keyboard better than her sister').

  • Superlatives and equality: 'as nicest as' is wrong because 'nicest' is a superlative. To show equality use the base adjective with 'as ... as' (example: 'as nice as').

  • Quick tip: Choose 'as well as' here if you mean that both Gauri and her sister can play the keyboard. If you want to say Gauri is better, use 'better than'.

title: Pen Write Knife Which one of the following options maintains
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Pen : Write :: Knife : _________

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above?
solution:
Answer: Cut

Explanation: The analogy pairs a tool with the action it performs. A pen is used to write; similarly, a knife is used to cut.

  • Cut — Correct: both pen and knife are tools paired with the verbs describing their function (write, cut).

  • Vegetables — Incorrect: this is an object that a knife might act on, not the action the knife performs.

  • Sharp — Incorrect: this is an attribute of a knife, not the action (function) of the knife.

  • Blunt — Incorrect: another attribute (opposite of sharp), not the action performed by the tool.

Tip: For analogies, first identify the type of relationship (function, object, attribute, cause, etc.), then choose the option that matches that same relation.

title: Listening to music during exercise improves exercise performance and reduces
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Listening to music during exercise improves exercise performance and reduces discomfort. Scientists researched whether listening to music while studying can help students learn better and the results were inconclusive. Students who needed external stimulation for studying fared worse while students who did not need any external stimulation benefited from music.

Which one of the following statements is the CORRECT inference of the above passage?

options.html: Listening to music has no effect on learning and a positive effect on physical exercise.
Listening to music has a clear positive effect both on physical exercise and on learning.
Listening to music has a clear positive effect on physical exercise. Music has a positive effect on learning only in some students.
Listening to music has a clear positive effect on learning in all students. Music has a positive effect only in some students who exercise.

solution:
Key idea: music clearly helps physical exercise, but its effect on learning is mixed and depends on the type of student.

  • Physical exercise: The passage states that listening to music during exercise improves performance and reduces discomfort, so there is a clear positive effect on exercise.

  • Learning: The studies were inconclusive overall. The passage specifies that students who needed external stimulation for studying fared worse with music, while students who did not need external stimulation benefited.

  • Combined inference: Therefore the correct conclusion is that music has a clear positive effect on physical exercise, and it has a positive effect on learning only for some students (those who did not require external stimulation).

Why other conclusions are wrong:

  • Claiming music has no effect on learning contradicts the evidence that some students benefited while others did worse.

  • Claiming a clear positive effect on learning for all students ignores the reported differences between students who needed external stimulation and those who did not.

  • Any statement that reverses which students benefit or ties learning benefits only to exercisers misreads the passage.

title: The is too high for it to be considered
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The _________ is too high for it to be considered _________.
solution:
The correct sentence is:

“The fare is too high for it to be considered fair.”

  • Fare means the amount charged for a journey, especially by bus, train, taxi, etc.

  • Fair means reasonable, just, or acceptable.

Therefore, the first blank requires fare because it refers to a price or charge, while the second blank requires fair because it describes whether that price is reasonable.

title: We reached the station late, and missed the train.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: We reached the station late, and _______ missed the train.
solution:
Answer: 'nearly'

Explanation: The sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb 'missed' and express that the action was almost true. 'Nearly' is an adverb meaning 'almost', so it correctly conveys 'almost missed the train.'

  • Why 'near' is wrong: 'Near' is a preposition or adjective (for example, 'near the station') and does not function as an adverb to modify 'missed'.

  • Why 'utterly' is wrong: 'Utterly' means 'completely' and would imply you totally missed the train, which is the opposite of 'almost missed'.

  • Why 'mostly' is wrong: 'Mostly' means 'for the most part' or 'generally' and does not express the idea of 'almost' in this context.

Example sentence: We reached the station late, and nearly missed the train.

title: Kind Often Frequently (By word meaning)
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Kind : _______ : : Often : Frequently

(By word meaning)
solution: Frequently is synonym of often, similarly, type is synonym of kind

title: The country of Zombieland is in distress since more than
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
The country of Zombieland is in distress since more than 75% of its working population is suffering from serious health issues. Studies conducted by competent health experts concluded that a complete lack of physical exercise among its working population was one of the leading causes of their health issues. As one of the measures to address the problem, the Government of Zombieland has decided to provide monetary incentives to those who ride bicycles to work.

Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following statements can be logically inferred with certainty?

options.html: All the working population of Zombieland will henceforth ride bicycles to work.
Riding bicycles will ensure that all of the working population of Zombieland is free of health issues.
The health experts suggested to the Government of Zombieland to declare riding bicycles as mandatory.
The Government of Zombieland believes that riding bicycles is a form of physical exercise.

solution:
Key inference: The government’s decision to provide monetary incentives for commuting by bicycle indicates it believes bicycle riding is a form of physical exercise that can help address the problem of lack of exercise.

  • Reason: The government introduced incentives specifically to encourage bicycle commuting as a measure to tackle health issues caused by lack of physical exercise. Choosing a measure that promotes cycling implies the government treats cycling as physical exercise.

  • Why the other statements are not certain:

  • There is no guarantee that all workers will ride bicycles; incentives encourage but do not ensure universal behavior change.

  • There is no basis to claim that riding bicycles will ensure all health problems disappear; lack of exercise is one leading cause, not necessarily the only cause, and 'ensure' implies a guaranteed cure which the passage does not support.

  • There is no statement that health experts recommended making bicycle riding mandatory; the passage only reports study findings and the government’s chosen incentive policy.

Conclusion: The only statement that can be logically inferred with certainty from the given information is that the government believes riding bicycles is a form of physical exercise.

title: Which one of the following sentence sequences creates coherent narrative?
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Which one of the following sentence sequences creates a coherent narrative?


(i) Once on the terrace, on her way to her small room in the corner, she notices the man right away.
(ii) She begins to pant by the time she has climbed all the stairs.
(iii) Mina has bought vegetables and rice at the market, so her bags are heavy.
(iv) He was leaning against the parapet, watching the traffic below.
solution:
Correct order and explanation:

  • Mina has bought vegetables and rice at the market, so her bags are heavy.

  • She begins to pant by the time she has climbed all the stairs.

  • Once on the terrace, on her way to her small room in the corner, she notices the man right away.

  • He was leaning against the parapet, watching the traffic below.

Why this order is coherent:

  • The sentence about buying groceries establishes the cause (heavy bags).

  • The panting follows as a natural effect of carrying heavy bags up the stairs, preserving cause-effect logic.

  • Arriving on the terrace and noticing the man follows chronologically and allows the final sentence to describe the man she has just seen.

Why the other orders are less coherent:

  • Putting the panting before the explanation that her bags are heavy reverses cause and effect and weakens the logical flow.

  • Introducing the man before establishing Mina's arrival or her reason for being out of breath makes his appearance feel unmotivated.

In short: place the explanation of the heavy bags first, then the panting caused by carrying them, then her arrival and noticing the man, and finally the description of the man.

title: If denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [dry → arid → parched] is analogous to [diet → fast → ________ ]. Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
solution:
Answer: starve

Explanation: The sequence [dry → arid → parched] shows increasing intensity of the same quality (dryness). We need a similar three-word progression for lack of food where the words increase in intensity.

  • diet — mild restriction of food (lowest intensity)

  • fast — voluntarily abstain from eating for a period (greater intensity)

  • starve — suffer extreme or prolonged lack of food (highest intensity)

Therefore, starve best completes the analogy because it matches the pattern of increasing intensity. The other choices either have opposite meanings or are unrelated to degrees of food deprivation.

title: In the given text, the blanks are numbered (i)−(iv). Select
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
In the given text, the blanks are numbered (i)−(iv). Select the best match for all the blanks.

Steve was advised to keep his head   ___(i)___before heading  ___(ii)___to bat; for, while he had a head ___(iii)___batting, he could only do so with a cool head ___(iv)___his shoulders.
solution:
Correct answer: (i) down (ii) out (iii) for (iv) on

  • Blank (i): "keep his head down" is the correct collocation meaning to lower or steady one’s head or to avoid drawing attention.

  • Blank (ii): "heading out to bat" is the natural expression for going out to take one’s turn at batting.

  • Blank (iii): "a head for batting" means an aptitude or knack for batting; "a head on batting" would not be idiomatic.

  • Blank (iv): "a cool head on his shoulders" is the standard idiom meaning he can remain calm; "for his shoulders" is incorrect here.

Putting these together gives: "Steve was advised to keep his head down before heading out to bat; for, while he had a head for batting, he could only do so with a cool head on his shoulders."

title: If denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [walk → jog → sprint] is analogous to [bothered → ________ → daunted].

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
solution:
Answer: fazed

Reason: The two sequences show a rise in intensity. Match the middle word by meaning so that it sits between the first and last in strength.

  • In the example with movement, walk → jog → sprint shows increasing intensity of speed.

  • We need a word that fits between "bothered" (mild upset) and "daunted" (intimidated/overwhelmed).

  • "fazed" means disturbed or unsettled — stronger than being merely bothered but not as extreme as being daunted.

Why the other choices are incorrect:

  • "phased" refers to stages or being carried out in phases; it does not mean upset or intimidated.

  • "phrased" relates to wording or expression and is unrelated to emotional intensity.

  • "fused" means joined or melted together and does not describe an emotional state.

title: Sequence the following sentences in coherent passage. This fortuitous geological
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.

P: This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the contact zone.

Q: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological event rather than as a static geological feature.

R: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and making it better suited for life.

S: Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
solution:
Correct coherent order and explanation:

  • Begin with the cause: Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.

  • Describe the immediate effect: This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the contact zone.

  • Give the longer-term consequence: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and making it better suited for life.

  • Conclude with the interpretation: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological event rather than as a static geological feature.

Why this order works: It follows a logical sequence from cause to immediate effect to long-term consequence and ends with the interpretive conclusion that summarizes the significance.

title: If denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [sick → infirm → moribund] is analogous to [silly → _______ → daft].

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
solution:
Key idea: identify an increasing-intensity relationship and apply it to the second list.

Explanation of the first sequence:

  • sick = mildly ill

  • infirm = more seriously ill or weak

  • moribund = at the point of death (most severe)

Apply the same pattern to the second sequence:

  • silly = mildly foolish

  • vain = used here to indicate a stronger degree of senselessness or pointless/showy behavior (more foolish than "silly" but not the strongest term)

  • daft = very foolish (most extreme)

Conclusion: "vain" is the best fit as the middle term because the analogy requires a word stronger than "silly" but weaker than "daft".

title: Thousands of years ago, some people began dairy farming. This
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: Inference-Based Questions, Assumption and Implication Recognition
text:
Thousands of years ago, some people began dairy farming. This coincided with a number of mutations in a particular gene that resulted in these people developing the ability to digest dairy milk.

Based on the given passage, which of the following can be inferred?

options.html: All human beings can digest dairy milk.
No human being can digest dairy milk.
Digestion of dairy milk is essential for human beings.
In human beings, digestion of dairy milk resulted from a mutated gene.

solution:
Correct inference: The passage supports that some people developed the ability to digest dairy milk because of mutations in a gene that appeared when dairy farming began.

  • Statement 'All human beings can digest dairy milk.' is not supported because the passage mentions only some people developed the ability, not all humans.

  • Statement 'No human being can digest dairy milk.' is contradicted by the passage, which says some people acquired the ability.

  • Statement 'Digestion of dairy milk is essential for human beings.' goes beyond the information given; the passage does not claim that milk digestion is essential.

  • Statement 'Digestion of dairy milk resulted from a mutated gene.' matches the passage's main point: mutations coincided with dairy farming and produced the ability to digest milk in people.

Why this is the best inference: The passage explicitly connects the emergence of dairy farming with genetic mutations that led to the ability to digest milk. That linkage supports the inference that the digestive ability resulted from a mutated gene, with the important nuance that this change applied to some people or populations rather than universally to all humans.

title: Ravi had younger brother who taught at university. He was
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Ravi had ______ younger brother who taught at ______ university. He was widely regarded as ______ honorable man.

Select the option with the correct sequence of articles to fill in the blanks.
solution:
Answer: a; a; an

Filled sentence: Ravi had a younger brother who taught at a university. He was widely regarded as an honorable man.

  • First blank: use "a" because "younger" begins with a consonant sound (/j/), so "a younger brother" is correct.

  • Second blank: use "a" before "university" because the word begins with the consonant sound /j/ (so the choice depends on pronunciation, not the first letter).

  • Third blank: use "an" before "honorable" because the initial "h" is silent and the word begins with a vowel sound, so "an honorable man" is correct.

Tip: choose "a" or "an" based on the initial sound of the following word. Use "the" only when referring to something specific or already mentioned.

title: The CEO’s decision to downsize the workforce was considered myopic
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
The CEO’s decision to downsize the workforce was considered myopic because it sacrificed long-term stability to accommodate short-term gains.

Select the most appropriate option that can replace the word “myopic” without changing the meaning of the sentence.
solution:
Answer: shortsighted

"Myopic" means lacking long-term perspective or foresight, focusing instead on immediate results. In the sentence, the CEO sacrificed long-term stability for short-term gains, which shows a short-term focus.

  • Why "shortsighted" is correct: "shortsighted" directly matches the idea of prioritizing short-term benefits over future stability.

  • Why "visionary" is wrong: "visionary" means far-sighted and forward-looking, the opposite of "myopic."

  • Why "progressive" is wrong: "progressive" implies moving forward or favoring reform, not lacking foresight.

  • Why "innovative" is wrong: "innovative" describes creativity or new methods, and does not convey short-term thinking.

Conclusion: "shortsighted" best preserves the original meaning of "myopic" as used in the sentence.

title: Put the brown paper in my pocket along with the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
subtopic: True / False / Cannot Say Type Questions
text:
“I put the brown paper in my pocket along with the chalks, and possibly other things. I suppose every one must have reflected how primeval and how poetical are the things that one carries in one’s pocket: the pocket-knife, for instance the type of all human tools, the infant of the sword. Once I planned to write a book of poems entirely about the things in my pocket. But I found it would be too long: and the age of the great epics is past.”

(From G.K. Chesterton’s “A Piece of Chalk”)

Based only on the information provided in the above passage, which one of the following statements is true?

options.html: The author of the passage carries a mirror in his pocket to reflect upon things.
The author of the passage had decided to write a poem on epics.
The pocket-knife is described as the infant of the sword.
Epics are described as too inconvenient to write.

solution:
Answer: The pocket-knife is described as the infant of the sword.

Explanation: The passage explicitly calls the pocket-knife "the infant of the sword," so the statement that the pocket-knife is described in that way is directly supported by the text.

  • The claim that the author carries a mirror to reflect upon things is not supported: the passage lists brown paper, chalks, and the pocket-knife and uses the verb "reflected" to mean people have thought about the pocket contents, not that a mirror is carried.

  • The claim that the author had decided to write a poem on epics is incorrect: the passage says he planned a book of poems about the things in his pocket, and separately notes that "the age of the great epics is past," so epics are not presented as his intended subject.

  • The claim that epics are described as too inconvenient to write is incorrect: the passage says the planned pocket-themed book "would be too long" and that the age of great epics is past, but it does not describe epics as inconvenient to write.

title: Despite his initial hesitation, Rehman’s to contribute to the success
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Despite his initial hesitation, Rehman’s _________ to contribute to the success of the project never wavered.

Select the most appropriate option to complete the above sentence.
solution:
Correct answer: resolve

Explanation: Resolve means firm determination. The sentence expresses that although Rehman hesitated at first, his determination to contribute remained steady. "Resolve to contribute" is a natural collocation and accurately conveys this meaning.

  • ambivalence: Means mixed or conflicting feelings. Using it here would imply persistent indecision, which does not match the intended contrast and is less natural grammatically (we usually say "ambivalence about contributing").

  • satisfaction: Means contentment or pleasure; it does not express persistence or determination and does not fit the sentence meaning or common phrasing.

  • resolve: Correct choice. It clearly denotes steady determination and fits the structure "his resolve to [do something] never wavered."

  • revolve: A verb meaning to move in a circle or to center on something; it is irrelevant to the intended meaning and ungrammatical in this context.

Tip: Look for a word that expresses steady determination and fits the collocation "to contribute." That will help you choose the most appropriate option.

Bird : Nest :: Bee : _______

title: The antonym of the word protagonist is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The antonym of the word protagonist is ________.
solution:
The correct answer is:

B) antagonist

Explanation:

  • A protagonist is the main or central character in a story (usually the hero).

  • An antagonist is the character who opposes the protagonist (often the villain).

Why others are incorrect:

  • Agnostic – someone unsure about religious beliefs

  • Arsonist – a person who sets fires

  • Anarchist – someone who opposes authority/government

So, the antonym of protagonist is antagonist

text:

solution: In indirect speech, the reporting verb remains in the past, the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he,' the simple past 'did' changes to past perfect 'had done,' and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before.'

subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Exacerbate : Mitigate :: ___________

Choose the option with the correct pair of words to fill the blank.
solution: Exacerbate means to make a problem or condition worse, while mitigate means to make it less severe. The analogous pair should therefore pair a word meaning to worsen with a word meaning to reduce severity.

subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
“He often _____ the numbers. False claims are not going to help. Honesty _____ trust”, said the manager.

Choose the option with the correct order of words to fill the blanks.
solution: The first blank requires a verb that can describe overstating numerical figures, and the second requires a verb meaning to produce or give rise to trust. “Exaggerates” and “engenders” satisfy these meanings.

subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Charity : P :: Retaliation : Q

Choose the appropriate pair of words P and Q that fit the analogy.

subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: ‘The team ______ more than 300 runs in 20 overs ___________ rains. However, some players needed to improve their batting skills.’ Choose the option with the correct sequence of words to fill the blanks.
solution: The sentence requires a finite past-tense verb for the completed action and a preposition meaning 'in spite of' before the noun phrase 'rains.' 'scored' provides the past-tense verb, and 'despite' introduces the contrasting condition.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q6
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: ‘People are crowding around ___ pit into which ___ elephant has fallen. I have never seen an elephant looking more bewildered ___ miserable. Here it is in a most undignified position, thrust into a pit and made to look up ___ a vast, curiosity-stricken crowd.’ Choose the option with the correct sequence of words to fill the blanks.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q2
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: The statements (S1), (S2), and (S3) pertain to the scores obtained by students in an exam. The maximum possible marks in the exam is 150. (S1) The highest score is 100. (S2) The fourth highest score is 76. (S3) There are at least four students whose scores are within 25 of each other. Which one of the following options is necessarily correct?
solution: Arrange the scores in nonincreasing order. If the highest score is 100 and the fourth highest score is 76, then the first four scores lie between 76 and 100. Their maximum difference is 24, so those four students have scores within 25 of each other.
